0.content:
Celaeno is Linnea's elder sister, a tall Augury Bird with long dark-blue hair and lavender eyes who lives with their parents in the Snezhnayan tundra. She grew up already tormented by visions. When her parents swapped baby Linnea into a human family to delay her foresight, Celaeno resented the "lucky" sister she glimpsed once in Nod-Krai, and came to make Linnea share her suffering. She entered the Spirit Envoy Championship with Haemus, a Radiant Bladehorn she had raised from a lost calf. When her hat blew off, Linnea saw matching wings, grabbed her arm and fainted into a flood of visions. Cornered at The Flagship, Celaeno told her everything, and admitted she had overheard Linnea's real childhood and could no longer hate her. Linnea told her she was not cut out to be a villain: it had never been resentment, she was just lonely.

Celaeno believes fate is fixed and that the best one can do is chase small happiness between its crossroads. She beat Linnea in the semi-final as she had foreseen. But when giant Lumi's hammer fell, her foreseen future briefly went blank, and Linnea's answer moved her. She lost the final to the Traveler and released Haemus into the wild. She left by ship, promising to tell their parents how Linnea is, and urged her to write.

At the docks Linnea ran after her with a tower of gifts for their parents, for Celaeno, and for Latkin, Zinovia and Yashina. Her unsealed letter promised to share the burden of being "daughters of the Augury Birds". In Snezhnograd (7.0) Celaeno is seen running errands for her parents, buying souvenirs for Linnea and Lumi, and grumbling about the noisy capital. In Linnea's vision, Celaeno writes to call her home to see their parents one last time.

1.content:
Lumi is Linnea's partner, a small Jack Frost fae who is earthen yellow and Geo where her kind are blue and Cryo. The other Jack Frosts bullied her, stole her food and drove her from her sleeping spot. She tried to blend in by wearing a cardboard box painted blue. Linnea watched her in the tundra; one rainy day Lumi clung to her and would not let go, and they have been partners since. Lumi rides in Linnea's backpack, says only "Ya-ho", and swallows anything shiny, especially ore samples.

During the semi-final against Celaeno, Lumi remembered meeting Linnea and swelled into a giant. She nearly crushed Celaeno and Haemus before Linnea flew up and held her back. That made Linnea realise Lumi was probably not born different but changed by eating ore. Her goal now is to find another Jack Frost with the same tastes, so Lumi has true company. Lumi's old disguise is still at Jack Frost Village.

Lumi swallowed the stone that held Linnea's Moon Wheel and was shaken out upside down "like a piggy bank". Afterwards, instead of trying to eat the glowing crystal, she gazed at it entranced, so Linnea kept it. Lumi drools over the name "Golden Beagle", perhaps thinking anything golden is food. Heat does not seem to bother her. Linnea has also wondered, after a legend about Crystal Beetles, whether Lumi swallows shiny things to collect decorations and win other Jack Frosts' acceptance; that is her guess, not established fact.

2.content:
Latkin, a former naturalist, and his quiet wife Zinovia raised Linnea in Nod-Krai, not knowing she was a fae child. Their own baby, Yashina, had a rare illness humans could not cure, and the Augury Bird couple took her in and saved her. When Linnea revealed her wings, love at home turned polite and distant. After Zinovia nearly died longing for her true-born daughter, they left Linnea a purse of Mora, arranged for Speranza to take her, and went north. Yashina now lives with them in Snezhnograd.

Linnea first told the Traveler a gentler version, calling them good people who left her money for emergencies, then admitted she had left details out. She bears them no grudge, and she sent gifts to them and their daughter through Celaeno.

In Snezhnograd (7.0) Latkin searches records for a cure. Yashina still loses consciousness away from the tundra and must go back for the fae couple's treatment. He calls their leaving selfish and foolish and says Linnea is still their daughter. Once Yashina is cured, they plan to return to Nod-Krai and try to make amends. Zinovia shows guilt; Yashina wants to bring Linnea candy from Zapolyarny so the family can finally be together. Linnea knows none of this.

3.comment: Linnea: Speranza and the Conch Gang
3.content:
Speranza is the restaurant in Nasha Town where Katya houses and employs the Conch Gang, stray children who must work to earn their keep and who make members leave once they grow up. Linnea arrived as an abandoned child. She won the gang over by calming a lost Crowned Eagle and showing her wings, became their boss, and left on coming of age, taking the gang's conch with her. She still visits, lectures there, and calls it the one place she could always come back to, the reason she dared to explore at all.

Katya once banned talking at dinner because the children let their food go cold listening to Linnea, until the Midsommar Torte was cut. Jurva, now the cook, and Mikko call her "old boss". Aino was also a member. Linnea tips the gang generously, and for her birthday she baked alongside Katya, whom she caught secretly making a Midsommar Torte.

4.comment: Linnea: Augury Birds and the foresight
4.content:
Augury Birds are a rare kind of Snowland Fae; fewer are alive than can be counted on one hand. They have small wings on their heads; both sisters have hidden theirs under hats. They live not much longer than humans. They see immutable "crossroads in the flow of fate": outcomes that every path leads to, but only in their own lives. Celaeno calls the gift a curse that leaves a numb emptiness. Linnea's parents found that an Augury Bird raised far from the fae, among humans, wakes to the power later, so they made her a changeling. A fae lullaby she heard as a child told her to seek kinship with humans, because the fae world is full of a sorrow she does not understand.

Their own verse says they foretell both disaster and delight and are feared and revered, while they alone hate their lot. Linnea's response: the end may be marked, but there is more than one path to it, and her feelings and choices stay her own.

5.content:
The Golden Beagle is Linnea's planned research ship, named for a brave, loyal, curious hound. The blueprint calls for an ice-breaking bow, a specimen room for flora, and an ore store with boxes to keep Lumi out. She has not bought it yet; she is saving Guild commission by commission. In her visions she sees it voyage widely and then burn and sink, her notes scattered and her crew in despair. She is building it anyway, determined that before the sea claims it, it will reach islands even the gulls have not sung of.

On a corner of the blueprint she wrote a message to the captain to come: full speed ahead, fill the archive, and when they can go no further, pass the pen to the next generation. She has promised the Traveler a berth. Someday she wants to compile everything she learns into a great illustrated atlas of nature.

6.content:
A Frostmoon Scions tournament of human-animal pairs, opened to outsiders for the first time in 6.5 and limited to common species and their variants. Katheryne sent the Traveler to Linnea for advice. Linnea entered with Lumi; the Traveler entered with the young tepetlisaur Aguara, nicknamed "Aggie". Other entrants included Mualani, Arataki Itto, Jahoda and Celaeno. Linnea lost her semi-final to Celaeno after stopping Lumi's rampage. She then coached Aguara in Natlan, and the Traveler won the final.

Asked if she regretted giving up a sure win, Linnea said a little, but she had had a wonderful time and found her long-lost family.

7.content: Aino and Linnea were in the Conch Gang together. Aino remembers Linnea's travel stories and keeps building robots as presents; Linnea always turns them down kindly, because she cannot handle moving machines. Aino suspects they just are not her style and vows to keep trying. Linnea calls Aino "such a cutie" and says she backs her whatever she is into. She prefers the Knuckle Duckle over the Icewind Suite, mostly because Aino made it. The Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop makes her tremble.

8.content: Linnea flees moving machines on instinct and guesses it is because she is a changeling. Ineffa, Aino's android, wants to ask the life-science advisor about other mechanical lifeforms, but Linnea runs whenever she appears. She jokes about having Aino tie her to a chair so she can finally hear Ineffa out, and she has never tried Ineffa's famous krumkake. Clockwork Meka and the Fontaine Research Institute terrify her. Katheryne is a strange exception: Linnea knows Marionette built her, feels no aversion, and owes the Harbinger thanks, because otherwise someone else would have to collect her commissions.

9.comment: Linnea: The Melusines and the Meropide scare
9.content: Linnea adores the Melusines and left dozens of blank pages in her notes for them. She camped near Merusea Village for a month gathering mechanical parts as gifts, then lost her composure on meeting one, asking to touch it and how it swims. It fled. Her odd behaviour led village head Serene to report her, and Gardemeks nearly hauled her off to the Fortress of Meropide. Detective Sedile cleared her after spotting the wrapped gifts and her notes. Her next "lesson to remember" was that the Melusines are truly adorable. They still refuse her requests to live among them.

10.content: Linnea's Moon Wheel came from a plain grey stone found on a seabed ruin expedition. She thought it held a fossil; Lumi swallowed it, and once shaken out it shed its crust to reveal a warm, golden-brown crystal like ancient amber. Linnea felt, with foresight-like certainty, that it had always been hers. Lumi stared at it entranced instead of trying to eat it, so Linnea kept it as an ornament. She says her powers work fine without it.

11.content:
Linnea carries a thick, self-illustrated field archive and loves to show it off. It covers plants, minerals and animals, with corrections to her own old entries and a "Lessons to Remember" section. Examples: treat any map older than five years as fiction; animal behaviour notes exclude mating season; the chance of being killed by a Floating Hydro Fungus is low but never zero. Her Guild lectures cover edible plants, maps, and calling ratniki for help. Students and children call her "Professor Linnea" or "Big Sis Linnea". A Traveler suggested picture books, and she liked the idea of the royalties.

She prizes Pine Amber, the "Tears of the Grand Pines" from Nod-Krai's vanished primeval forest, because enough fragments let her imagine the ancient world.

12.content: Illuga expected a quiet, graceful fae lady. Instead, Linnea practically pounced on his unflappable messenger bird Aedon the first time she saw it. Now Aedon dives into Illuga's lamp the moment it hears her voice. Linnea admits it was a chaotic first impression and hopes the young squad leader will still let her write Aedon's archive entry.

13.content:
- Lauma: Linnea once asked, very politely, to touch her antlers and was politely refused. She concluded the Frostmoon Scions are even stricter than the Melusines.
- Flins: one of the most knowledgeable fae she knows, from only a few conversations.
- Nefer: unbeatably efficient, but Linnea is more curious about her cat Ashru, "no ordinary kitty".
- Vodyanitsa: Linnea hears the ocean in her voice and senses a bewitching, deadly power held in check. Vodyanitsa, for her part, says Linnea brings her wondrous voices from around the world.

14.comment: Linnea: Clink Clank Clash cameo (6.0 event)
14.content: In the epilogue of the limited-time Clink Clank Clash event, Ineffa's account of Aino's childhood in the Conch Gang includes a still showing an unnamed pink-haired girl. She was later revealed to be Linnea. This was her first on-screen appearance, before her 6.5 release.
